title: Audit slice routing and fallback protocol (PRD draft)
body:
Context and motivation:

This is a working PRD sketch proposing an "audit-slice" model for audit logs and approval-evidence where customers run networking components (VPC / sidecars / edge adaptors). Goal: make forensic queries fast and robust while respecting customer-managed networking constraints (no central push of raw logs, optional escrow, hybrid read paths). Also tie audit evidence to approval gates so that every approval decision has verifiable, retrievable proof even if part of the evidence lives in customer-managed systems.

Why now:
- Increasing enterprise demand for private deployments where raw network telemetry cannot be exported by default.
- Current monolithic audit-store design causes expensive cross-tenant queries and brittle behavior when the customer-managed endpoint is slow/out.
- Customers ask for short-term guarantees (SLA) for audit retrieval during incident investigations and for legal e-discovery.

Proposal summary (high-level):
1) Audit slices: partition audit/evidence by logical groups (approval epochs, change bundles, operator session ids) and store a compact "slice header" in Redwood's immutable index. The slice header contains metadata, signatures, hash pointers, retention policy, and read-routing hints (customer-side vs redwood-replicated).
2) Dual-path reads and hedging: queries first consult Redwood index; index yields authoritative slice headers and preferred read endpoints. For each slice read, try the customer-managed endpoint (sidecar/edge-forwarder) in parallel with Redwood replica(s) based on a hedging policy. Use first-successful-response within SLO; if both slow, escalate to fallback protocol.
3) Fallback & escrow: when customer-managed endpoint is unreachable or fails attestation checks, Redwood can return an "escrowed snapshot" previously synchronized (if customer opted in), or mark slice as "forensic-pending" and begin an evidence-request flow (automated operator ticket + customer webhook).
4) Approval-gate binding: approvals get cross-referenced to slices (approval-id -> slice-ids). Approval decisions include a compact proof token (signed by Redwood and optionally by customer HSM) and the slice headers required to rehydrate the evidence.

Key terms / invariants:
- Slice header: small immutable record (<= 4KB) persisted in Redwood control-plane index. Contains: slice-id, sequence-range, timestamps, retention-tier, primary-read-endpoint(s), content-hash, signature(s), approval-refs.
- Hedging policy: configurable per-customer SLO (fast, economical, forensic-safe). Determines parallelism (N endpoints, timeouts, backoff).
- Escrow snapshot: periodic compact bundle of evidence that customer permits Redwood to store encrypted in a segregated escrow store for retrieval under specified conditions.

Sequence example (operator changes a firewall rule):
- Operator creates change bundle -> approval workflow starts -> approval decisions produce approval-id A123.
- Sidecar collects network handshake traces + audit statements and anchors a slice S1. Sidecar signs S1 metadata and pushes slice header to Redwood index (no PII payload).
- If customer enabled escrow, sidecar uploads encrypted S1 payload to escrow bucket and sends manifest to Redwood index.
- Later, investigator requests logs for approval A123 -> Redwood looks up slice-ids [S1, S2]. Hedging kicks off: query to sidecar endpoint (fast-path) + query to Redwood replica (if present). First to return wins; if both fail, fallback engages.

Design constraints and decisions to discuss:
- Minimal index size: slice headers are deliberately small to keep the global index searchable and cheap. Full payloads may live on-customer, in escrow, or in Redwood cold-store depending on policy.
- Integrity: every slice header must include a content-hash and a signature from the origin (sidecar) to prevent tampering; Redwood will also sign the header on ingest.
- Privacy-by-default: do not replicate raw payloads without explicit opt-in. Escrow is opt-in per-customer per-retention-window.
- Atomicity across slices: approval binding must ensure that when an approval references multiple slices, it is possible to fetch a consistent snapshot (same logical time-window). We'll need a lightweight multi-slice manifest with monotonic epoch numbers.
- Cost trade-offs: hedging increases egress/cost but reduces latency and improves reliability. Expose cost-vs-latency knobs in Console.

Failure modes and recovery:
- Sidecar slow/unavailable: Redwood uses replicas or escrow. If no replica and no escrow, mark the request as "evidence-missing"; trigger auto-ticket to on-call SRE and notify customer via webhook and support channel.
- Divergent evidence/hashes: if payload hash doesn't match header -> preserve both payloads, mark slice conflicted, start integrity audit workflow (automatic diff + notify security).
- Customer revokes escrows: revocation should be recorded as a new slice header with revocation flag and retention timeline for any previously escrowed copies (legal constraints may require continued hold; need legal review).

Operational SLOs / metrics to track:
- P50/P95 audit-retrieval latency (fast-path and fallback path)
- Hedging success rate (percentage of reads satisfied by customer endpoint)
- Escrow retrieval latency and success rate
- Fraction of slices with signature verification failures
- Cost per retrieval (approx tokenized for billing)

Security / compliance notes:
- Signatures must support customer-key attestation (KMS/HSM) — design hooks for customer-signed headers.
- Audit index must support tamper-evidence and append-only semantics; retention/release flows must be auditable.
- Provide configurable retention tiers: ephemeral (7–30d), standard (90–365d), legal-hold (custom).

UX / API surface (sketch):
- In Console: approval detail page shows linked slices, state (available / escrowed / pending), retrieval button with preview and retrieval cost estimate.
- API: GET /v1/private/audit/slices/:slice_id -> returns header + read-endpoint(s); POST /v1/private/audit/retrieve -> returns streaming evidence or retrieval ticket.
- Webhooks: customer can register an evidence-delivery webhook (for asynchronous fallback).

Open questions / TODOs (rough):
- Legal: confirm escrow retention/transfer policies across regions and under subpoena. (Legal ticket: JIRA-PRIV-621)
- Integrity model: are sidecar signatures sufficient, or add a notarization step (trusted third-party) for high-sensitivity customers?
- UX: how to surface cost trade-offs without scaring product users? quick frictionless defaults needed.
- Performance: simulate hedging costs with current traffic mix; produce rough cost model. (Action: eng infra bench - @Eliot)
- Query semantics: support partial-slice reads and byte-range streaming for large forensic payloads.

Next milestones (proposal):
- Week 0–2: design review with infra/forensics/legal; finalize header schema and minimal API contract.
- Week 3–6: prototype index-only ingest + sidecar header push; local hedging simulation harness.
- Week 7–10: implement hedging client + fallback ticket flow; minimal Console UI for slice list.
- Week 11–14: integrate escrow store (encryption-at-rest), add retention controls and demo for two pilot customers.

Risks and mitigation:
- Customer distrust of escrow: provide strong encryption guarantees, allow customer-managed keys, and clear opt-in messaging.
- Increased operational complexity: keep index schema narrow; offload heavy payloads to customer or cold-store.
- Legal surprise: engage Legal early and design features to respect cross-border data controls.

Notes to self / shorthand:
- Keep headers tiny. E2E signing + monotonic epoch = minimal trust.
- Hedging policy needs to be tunable per-customer and per-workload. Default: try customer sidecar for 50ms, if no response, fall back to Redwood replica; if neither in 500ms, start escalation ticket.
- Consider a background "rehydration" job that opportunistically copies customer-chosen slices into escrow during low-cost windows (opt-in).

References / links (internal):
- earlier work: confluence://private-deployments/network-approval-ux-rollback-triggers (see approval binding section)
- infra benchmark plan: github.com/redwood-inference/private-deploy/bench/hedging-sims (WIP)

Immediate next steps (for this draft):
- Share with eng infra and applied-ml for comments (ask: ETA 1 week).
- Add header schema draft and example 3‑slice manifest (small JSON examples) into this doc.
- Draft a brief pilot checklist for two customers: one finance (strict retention/legal-hold), one fintech (HSM + low-latency).

Unresolved / discussion items (call to reviewers):
- Are we comfortable with indexing headers in the control plane by default? Privacy pros/cons?
- What is minimal telemetry we can collect for troubleshooting without exposing payloads?
- How to charge for hedged reads vs single-path reads?

-- end draft --

(Notes: this is intentionally rough; feel free to cut sections into separate PRDs — audit index schema, hedging client, escrow onboarding, approval binding schema)
